verses.1: Rama heard the entire piteous lamentation of that brahmin, which was filled with sorrow and grief.
verses.2: Distressed by sorrow, Rama summoned his ministers, along with Vasistha, Vamadeva, his two brothers, and the representatives of the city.
verses.3: Then, eight brahmins, accompanied by Vasistha, were ushered in and, seeing the god-like king, they blessed him saying, "May you prosper!"
verses.4: Markandeya, Maudgalya, Vamadeva, Kashyapa, Katyayana, Jabali, Gautama, and Narada—all these eminent brahmins were seated on their respective seats.
verses.5: With folded hands, Rama respectfully saluted the arrived great sages, as well as the ministers and citizens, each according to their due.
verses.6: Rama narrated everything to all those seated sages of shining splendor, explaining that this brahmin's situation was causing a hindrance.
verses.7: Having heard the distressed king's words, Narada replied with auspicious words to the king in the presence of the sages.
verses.8: O King, O Rama, listen to how the child's death occurred in due course, and having heard what is to be done, perform your duty.
verses.9: O King, in the ancient Krita Yuga, only brahmins were ascetics, and no non-brahmin was an ascetic by any means.
verses.10: In that resplendent, divine, and unobstructed age, all beings were born immortal and far-seeing.
verses.11: Thereafter, in the age named Treta Yuga, embodied humans, specifically Kshatriyas, were born endowed with complete penance.
verses.12: Those great-souled humans who were superior in valor and penance in their previous birth were indeed born in this Treta Yuga.
verses.13: All those Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, both the former and the latter, were endowed with equal valor in both ages.
verses.14: Not seeing any greater distinction among them, all of them then established the approved system of four varnas.
verses.15: In that brightly shining age, which was indeed full of unobstructed dharma, unrighteousness nevertheless placed one foot upon the surface of the earth.
verses.16: Indeed, one who is associated with unrighteousness will find their splendor diminished.
verses.17: That which was the object of desire for the ancients and a great passionate impurity, that very being named Untruth, manifested on the earth with one foot.
verses.18: Indeed, when untruth caused one foot of Dharma to fall due to unrighteousness, then the duration of life was previously determined and established.
verses.19: Indeed, even when that untruth and unrighteousness had descended upon the earth, people devoted to truth and righteousness still performed only auspicious deeds.
verses.20: In the Treta Yuga, all those Brahmins and Kshatriyas who existed performed penance, while other people performed service.
verses.21: That supreme righteousness, which was previously universal, now reached the Vaiśyas and Śūdras, and the Śūdras, in particular, began to perform worship for all castes.
verses.22: O best of kings, in this interval, as unrighteousness and falsehood increased among the people, the former state of righteousness greatly diminished.
verses.23: Then, unrighteousness manifested its second quarter, and consequently, this age came to be known as Dvāpara.
verses.24: O best of men, during the prevailing Dvāpara age, which marked a decline, both unrighteousness and falsehood greatly increased.
verses.25: In that age designated as Dvāpara, austerity entered the Vaiśyas, as indeed, austerity successively entered the three castes over the course of the three ages (Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara).
verses.26: For the three ages (Krita, Treta, Dvapara), dharma is established for the three higher varnas, and a Shudra does not obtain religious merit by performing penance in these ages; yet, O best of kings, a person of lower caste is performing very great penance.
verses.27: Indeed, the performance of penance by a Shudra will be permissible in the Kali Yuga, but in the Dvapara Yuga, O King, it is the greatest unrighteousness for one born as a Shudra.
verses.28: That very great ascetic, O King, is indeed performing penance today at the border of your kingdom, and it is by this foolish act that this child's death has occurred.
verses.29: Indeed, any evil-minded person who commits unrighteousness or an improper act, which is the root of misfortune, in the king's kingdom or city, quickly goes to hell, and so does the king, without a doubt.
verses.30: A king who protects his subjects righteously obtains a sixth share of the merit from their Vedic studies, penance, and good deeds.
verses.31: How can a king who does not protect his subjects be entitled to receive the sixth part of their produce as tax?
verses.32: O tiger among men, you should search your own kingdom, and wherever you find an evil deed, there you must make an effort to rectify it.
verses.33: O best of men, if this is done, there will be an increase in righteousness and the lifespan of men, and this child's life will also be restored. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुःसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 74 ।। Thus ends the seventy-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
